newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UK pledges effort to find Britons in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: UK pledges effort to find Britons in Chechnya.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook promised on Monday to leave no stone unturned in the search for two British aid workers kidnapped in Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya.
Cook discussed the disappearance of Camilla Carr and Jon James at a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and thanked Moscow for its help and understanding.
Carr and James were seized on July 3 from the house where they were staying by a group of armed, masked men.
Police have detained and interrogated several people the two Britons had been working with, including their bodyguards, but have reported no progress so far.
"The situation there is difficult and dangerous," Cook told a joint news conference with Primakov.
"I understand the feelings of Jon and Camilla's families and friends. We will continue to leave no stone unturned in our efforts to get them home safely," he added.
Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov last week ordered a special mobile investigative brigade to be set up, including judges of Islamic Sharia law, to tackle a wave of kidnappings sweeping the region.
Hostage-taking has become a huge problem in Chechnya, where Russian troops fought separatist forces for 21 months until last August.

The Britons had been working for the Centre for Peacemaking and Community Development, which is involved in the psychological rehabilitation of children affected by the conflict, in which tens of thousands of people died and many more were injured or made homeless.
Kidnappers usually ask for money for the return of their captives but there has been no word of any demands for the release of the Britons.
